structure.title: Shipwreck and disguise
structure.text: Viola's arrival creates an unequal distribution of knowledge within an already frustrated courtship.

structure.title: Interlocking performances
structure.text: Love messages, household jokes, and mistaken identities develop alongside one another, crossing pleasure with the risk of humiliation.

people.name: Olivia
people.text: A grieving woman resisting his attentions.

context.title: An audience with extra knowledge
context.text: A disguised identity lets one conversation mean different things to its participants. The audience can hear meanings some speakers miss.
context.takeaway: Track both the intended and received message.

context.title: Festivity and its costs
context.text: Drinking, music, and practical jokes challenge household discipline. Exclusion can also become entertainment for those inside the group.
context.takeaway: Ask when amusement requires a victim.

notice.text: Notice people enjoying their own descriptions of love.
notice.why: Self-presentation can compete with attention to the beloved.
Their passing time complicates the comedy's promises.

opening: Viola survives a shipwreck, disguises herself as a young man, and takes work carrying love messages for a duke. She falls for her employer; the woman receiving his messages falls for her. Nobody can speak plainly without endangering something, and everybody has a persuasive account of their own feelings. Shakespeare surrounds this triangle with drinking, music, vanity, and a practical joke that stops being harmless. Desire makes the characters inventive, while the audience enjoys the precarious privilege of knowing who is actually talking to whom.
